The setup is correct. Splitting after the k-th card gives P(k) = (10^k − 1)(10^(9−k) − 1), and P(k) = P(9−k), so the distinct products come from k = 1, 2, 3, 4. The sum is

S = 4(10^9 + 1) − 111,111,110 = 4,000,000,004 − 111,111,110 = 3,888,888,894.

The error is in the digit sum. S = 3,888,888,894 has 10 digits: 3, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 9, 4. That is seven 8s, not six. The sum is 3 + 56 + 9 + 4 = 72. The proposed solution counted only six 8s and got 64.

The correct answer is 72, so the stated answer of 64 is wrong.

VERDICT: REJECT
